newsitem.title: FINLAND: Imatran Voima sees operating profit, sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Imatran Voima sees operating profit, sales growth.

text.p: Finnish state-owned energy group Imatran Voima Oy (IVO) said on Thursday it expects growth in operating profit and turnover this year.
"Operating profit and turnover will continue to show growth during 1997," IVO CEO Kalevi Numminen said in a statement with the group's 1996 results.
In 1996, IVO's operating profit rose 53 percent to 2.04 billion markka and turnover increased 51 percent to 12.1 billion markka.
Numminen said the 1996 result had been good.

Earnings by the group's Swedish subsidiary Gullspangs Kraftaktiebolag and abundant electricity sales to the Norwegian-Swedish electricity bourse had had particularly positive effects on IVO's profit, it said.
The incorporation into IVO's full-year 1997 figures of Gullspang and of the Finnish subsidiary Lansivoima Oy would lead to growing group turnover, Numminen said.
But group profit after financial items would weaken somewhat due to higher financial costs after IVO's debts increased as a result of acquisitions.
